original_question: Let G be a subgroup of GL(n, Q) with finitely many orbits under automorphisms. Is G a virtually soluble group?
target_in_paper: Problem 21.40 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)" of Unsolved Problems in Group Theory. The Kourovka Notebook.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's official problem almost verbatim: it has the correct ambient linear group GL(n, Q), the correct hypothesis that G has finitely many orbits under automorphisms, and the correct conclusion asking whether G must be virtually soluble.
missing_details: Specify that n is a positive integer and G is a subgroup of GL_n(Q).
Clarify that "finitely many orbits under automorphisms" means finitely many orbits for the natural action of Aut(G) on the underlying set G.
Clarify that "virtually soluble" means that G has a soluble subgroup of finite index.
State explicitly that no additional hypotheses such as finite generation, torsion restrictions, or residual finiteness are assumed.
refined_question: Let n >= 1 and let G be a subgroup of GL_n(Q). Suppose that the natural action of Aut(G) on G has only finitely many orbits. Must G be virtually soluble; that is, must G contain a soluble subgroup of finite index?
justification: In the cited paper, the relevant target is exactly Problem 21.40, whose wording is essentially the same as your draft. The surrounding text does not add extra hypotheses or a sharper reformulation. The nearby Problem 21.39 uses the same phrase "finitely many orbits under automorphisms," which confirms that the intended condition is the standard automorphism-orbit condition for the action of Aut(G) on G. So the only real refinements needed are to make the action and the meaning of "virtually soluble" explicit and to note that no further assumptions are imposed.
